summary: An interactive browser-based 3D space mission simulator that lets beginners design, launch, and fly a spacecraft in 10 minutes, turning abstract aerospace trade-offs into hands-on engineering intuition.
details:
Overview & How It Works Mission Control: Beyond Earth is an interactive, browser-based 3D space mission simulator that lets users design, launch, and fly a spacecraft in 10 minutes. Instead of learning aerospace concepts in disconnected pieces, players go through a complete end-to-end mission lifecycle: choosing a science goal, assembling spacecraft subsystems, selecting an orbit and launch vehicle, piloting the mission through live hazards (such as solar storms), and reviewing an engineering debrief.
The simulation models real aerospace engineering trade-offs in an accessible way: solar power drops to 43% at Mars distance, launch mass scales to roughly 2× dry mass due to propellant requirements, communication data rates decrease with distance, and design margins determine whether the spacecraft survives space weather events. Rather than a simple pass/fail screen, players receive a detailed score out of 100 explaining the exact engineering reasons behind their mission’s success or failure.
Benefits & Intended Impact Space mission design is often taught in isolated modules, keeping the trade-offs between science payload, mass, power, and budget abstract, while professional engineering software is too complex for beginners. Our project provides a zero-install, zero-prerequisite educational tool for high school students, university freshmen, teachers, and space clubs. By making mistakes free and consequences immediately visible in 3D, learners build real systems-engineering intuition through a rapid design → fail → learn → redesign cycle.
Creativity & Design Considerations Unlike static quizzes or single-variable calculators, our simulator connects every subsystem dynamically—changing one component immediately impacts power budgets, mass limits, and survival odds. During development, our team prioritized accessibility (running smoothly in any standard web browser without installation), scientific honesty (grounding simplified formulas in real NASA mission architectures like LRO, MRO, and OSIRIS-REx), and clear visual feedback (such as flashing warning indicators in the builder).
Tools, Languages & Software Used
• Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3
• Frameworks & Libraries: React, Three.js (for 3D spacecraft and planetary visualization), Vite
• Hosting & Version Control: GitHub, GitHub Pages
• AI Tools: Claude (code generation assistance) and ChatGPT (initial concept brainstorming), with all physics formulas, UI/UX, and code reviewed, tested, and validated by the team.
